era_setting.place: West Warwick, Rhode Island, USA -- a single-storey wood-framed roadside nightclub, and the NIST fire laboratory in Gaithersburg, Maryland
era_setting.notes: The night is 20 February 2003. The film reaches back to a 1981 occupancy application and forward to the NIST report of June 2005. Early-2000s New England: 2003 cars, 2003 mobile phones, wood shingle siding, a gravel car park. Nothing from the 2010s or 2020s may appear as present day. This is a small American roadside building, not a city venue.

forbidden_claims: Anything about charges, pleas, sentences or convictions. Three living men were convicted in connection with this fire and the Rhode Island court record is source S3 in the facts ledger, which has NOT been opened. Until it is, no criminal outcome may appear on screen in any form.

That the band, or any member of it, caused the deaths. NCSTAR 2 records that a pyrotechnic ignited the foam (FACTS_LEDGER row ST-201). NIST's three direct contributors are the building contents, the inability to suppress the fire early, and the inability of the exits to handle the occupants (ST-602).
That the owners knew the foam was flammable. The record establishes how the foam behaved, not what any person knew.
That the fire department was slow or negligent. Nothing in NCSTAR 2 supports it. The first hose line is a timing fact (ST-309), not a finding.

Any occupant figure stated as established fact. ST-101 is a media range of 440 to 458 and ST-106 is an attribution to the Attorney General's office. The hard numbers are the 2003 model-code figure of about 420 (ST-102) and the paperwork trail of 225, 253 and 317 (ST-103 to ST-105).
That the exits were illegal or below the code in force. NIST says the 2003 model codes already had provisions addressing these problems (ST-603), which is not a finding that this building broke them.
That everyone could have escaped. NIST modelled a door twice as wide changing the number still inside at 90 seconds (ST-502). That is not a claim that all one hundred would have lived.
That the crowd panicked. ST-305 and ST-306 record a blockage and then a crush. NIST's own recommendation 8 states that crowd-crush behaviour is not yet understood (ST-607).

That 95 of the fatalities were due to inability to evacuate. That figure appears in NIST's public summary but was NOT located in Volume 1 by a space-insensitive search of the full text. Do not use it until it is found.
Anything about the site today, memorials, anniversaries, or the families.
Any name of any person who died. The names of the dead do not appear.

That the building was a firetrap or an accident waiting to happen. Those are characterisations. Report the foam test (ST-203, ST-204), the single doorway (ST-004) and the occupant paperwork (ST-103 to ST-105) and let them stand.

notes: EP81 of the EP77-82 slate. Runtime and word bands follow the owner's 2026-08-23 decision: 29-32 minutes, divided at the measured 160 wpm, never 176. Source is NIST NCSTAR 2 Volume 1, downloaded and read at 252 pages, page-cited in the facts ledger. TRAP recorded there: that PDF extracts with no spaces between words, so a normal keyword search finds almost nothing and reads as though the report never states the obvious -- every search must run against a space-stripped copy. The controlling idea, never spoken: a building holds as many people as its narrowest opening will let out. Motif: a doorway -- two doors from outside, one door from inside, empty, full, empty again. forbidden_subjects bans the fire itself in every form: no flames, no smoke-filled room, no crush, no burning building, no aftermath, no band on stage. The film is carried by a doorway, a sheet of foam, a floor plan, a stopwatch and a laboratory. R3 is heavy: one hundred people died and three living men were convicted, and the court record is not open, so no criminal outcome may appear until it is.
